	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map size must be at least 3x3");
		}
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
					cells[r][c] = new Wall(new Coordinate(r, c));
				} else {
					cells[r][c] = new FillableCell(new Coordinate(r, c));
				}
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		Coordinate sourceCoord = sourceInfo.coord;
		Direction sourceDir = sourceInfo.direction;
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceCoord, sourceDir, true);
		cells[sourceCoord.row][sourceCoord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo;
		do {
			sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		} while (sinkInfo.coord.equals(sourceCoord));
		Coordinate sinkCoord = sinkInfo.coord;
		Direction sinkDir = sinkInfo.direction;
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkCoord, sinkDir, false);
		cells[sinkCoord.row][sinkCoord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map size must be at least 3x3");
		}
		if (cells == null || cells.length != rows) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array row count mismatch");
		}
		for (Cell[] row : cells) {
			if (row == null || row.length != cols) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array column count mismatch");
			}
		}
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		TerminationCell foundSource = null;
		TerminationCell foundSink = null;
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				Cell cell = cells[r][c];
				if (cell == null) {
					throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at (" + r + "," + c + ") is null");
				}
				this.cells[r][c] = cell;
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tc) {
					Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(r, c);
					boolean isEdge = (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1);
					if (tc.isSource()) {

							throw new IllegalArgumentException(

							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source cells found");

						Coordinate adjacent = coord.add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (!isValidCoordinate(adjacent) || this.cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col] instanceof Wall) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException(
									"Source cell points into a wall or outside map at (" + r + "," + c + ")");
						}
						foundSource = tc;
					} else {
						if (!isEdge) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink cell must be on edge at (" + r + "," + c + ")");
						}
						Coordinate adjacent = coord.add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (isValidCoordinate(adjacent)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException(
									"Sink cell must point outside the map at (" + r + "," + c + ")");
						}
						if (foundSink != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink cells found");
						}
						foundSink = tc;
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (foundSource == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source cell found");
		}
		if (foundSink == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink cell found");
		}
		this.sourceCell = foundSource;

	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int r = row - 1;
		int c = col - 1;
		if (r < 0 || r >= rows || c < 0 || c >= cols) {
			return false;

		Cell cell = cells[r][c];

	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
		if (!isValidCoordinate(coord)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Coordinate out of map bounds: " + coord);
		}
		Cell cell = cells[coord.row][coord.col];
		if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at " + coord + " is not a FillableCell");
		}
		cells[coord.row][coord.col] = new FillableCell(coord);
	}

	public void fillTiles(int distance) {
		if (distance < 0 || sourceCell == null) {
			return;
		}
		filledTiles.clear();
		Queue<Map.Entry<Coordinate, Integer>> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Coordinate start = sourceCell.coord;
		queue.add(Map.entry(start, 0));
		filledTiles.add(start);
		sourceCell.setFilled();
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Map.Entry<Coordinate, Integer> entry = queue.poll();
			Coordinate coord = entry.getKey();
			int dist = entry.getValue();
			if (dist >= distance) {
				continue;
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = coord.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (!isValidCoordinate(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				if (filledTiles.contains(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell cell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
				if (cell instanceof FillableCell fillableCell) {
					fillableCell.setFilled();
					filledTiles.add(neighbor);
					queue.add(Map.entry(neighbor, dist + 1));
				} else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell terminationCell) {
					terminationCell.setFilled();
					filledTiles.add(neighbor);
					queue.add(Map.entry(neighbor, dist + 1));
				}
			}
		}
	}

	public boolean checkPath() {
		if (sourceCell == null || sinkCell == null) {
			return false;
		}
		Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		queue.add(sourceCell.coord);
		visited.add(sourceCell.coord);
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			if (current.equals(sinkCell.coord)) {
				return true;
			}
			Cell currentCell = cells[current.row][current.col];
			if (!(currentCell instanceof FillableCell || currentCell instanceof TerminationCell)) {
				continue;
			}
			Pipe currentPipe = null;
			if (currentCell instanceof FillableCell fillableCell) {
				currentPipe = fillableCell.getPipe();
			} else if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
				currentPipe = null;
			}
			List<Direction> directionsToCheck = new ArrayList<>();
			if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell terminationCell) {
				directionsToCheck.add(terminationCell.getDirection());
			} else if (currentPipe != null) {
				directionsToCheck.addAll(currentPipe.getConnectedDirections());
			} else {
				continue;
			}
			for (Direction dir : directionsToCheck) {
				Coordinate neighborCoord = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (!isValidCoordinate(neighborCoord) || visited.contains(neighborCoord)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell neighborCell = cells[neighborCoord.row][neighborCoord.col];
				if (!(neighborCell instanceof FillableCell || neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell)) {
					continue;
				}
				Pipe neighborPipe = null;
				if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell fillableCell) {
					neighborPipe = fillableCell.getPipe();
					if (neighborPipe == null) {
						continue;
					}
				} else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell neighborTermination) {
					if (!neighborTermination.getDirection().equals(dir.getOpposite())) {
						continue;
					}
				}
				if (neighborPipe != null && !neighborPipe.getConnectedDirections().contains(dir.getOpposite())) {
					continue;
				}
				visited.add(neighborCoord);
				queue.add(neighborCoord);
			}
		}
		return false;
	}

package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import game.map.cells.Wall;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;
import util.StringUtils;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {

	private final int rows;
	private final int cols;
	@NotNull
	final Cell[][] cells;

	private TerminationCell sourceCell;
	private TerminationCell sinkCell;

	@NotNull
	private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
	private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
	private Integer prevFilledDistance;

	/**
	 * Constructs a map from a map string.
	 * <p>
	 * This is a convenience method for unit testing.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rows     Number of rows.
	 * @param cols     Number of columns.
	 * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
	 * @return A map with the cells set from {@code cellsRep}.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the map is incorrectly formatted.
	 */
	@NotNull
	static Map fromString(int rows, int cols, @NotNull String cellsRep) {
		var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);

		return new Map(rows, cols, cells);
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col).
	 *
	 * @param coord Coordinate to place pipe at.
	 * @param pipe  Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return {@code true} if the pipe is placed in the cell, {@code false} otherwise.
	 */
	public boolean tryPlacePipe(@NotNull final Coordinate coord, @NotNull final Pipe pipe) {
		return tryPlacePipe(coord.row, coord.col, pipe);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	/**
	 * Displays the current map.
	 */
	public void display() {
		final int padLength = Integer.valueOf(rows - 1).toString().length();

		Runnable printColumns = () -> {
			System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			System.out.print(' ');
			for (int i = 0; i < cols - 2; ++i) {
				System.out.print((char) ('A' + i));
			}
			System.out.println();
		};

		printColumns.run();

		for (int i = 0; i < rows; ++i) {
			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(String.format("%1$" + padLength + "s", i));
			} else {
				System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			}

			Arrays.stream(cells[i]).forEachOrdered(elem -> System.out.print(elem.toSingleChar()));

			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(i);
			}

			System.out.println();
		}

		printColumns.run();
	}

	public void fillBeginTile() {
		sourceCell.setFilled();
	}

	@NotNull
	private List<Coordinate> getTraversedCoords() {
		return new ArrayList<>(filledTiles);
	}

	public boolean hasLost() {

	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map size must be at least 3x3");
		}
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
					cells[r][c] = new Wall(new Coordinate(r, c));
				} else {
					cells[r][c] = new FillableCell(new Coordinate(r, c));
				}
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		Coordinate sourceCoord = sourceInfo.coord;
		Direction sourceDir = sourceInfo.direction;
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceCoord, sourceDir, true);
		cells[sourceCoord.row][sourceCoord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo;
		do {
			sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		} while (sinkInfo.coord.equals(sourceCoord));
		Coordinate sinkCoord = sinkInfo.coord;
		Direction sinkDir = sinkInfo.direction;
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkCoord, sinkDir, false);
		cells[sinkCoord.row][sinkCoord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map size must be at least 3x3");
		}
		if (cells == null || cells.length != rows) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array row count mismatch");
		}
		for (Cell[] row : cells) {
			if (row == null || row.length != cols) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array column count mismatch");
			}
		}
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		TerminationCell foundSource = null;
		TerminationCell foundSink = null;
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				Cell cell = cells[r][c];
				if (cell == null) {
					throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at (" + r + "," + c + ") is null");
				}
				this.cells[r][c] = cell;
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tc) {
					Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(r, c);
					boolean isEdge = (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1);
					if (tc.isSource()) {
						if (isEdge) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException(
									"Source cell cannot be on edge at (" + r + "," + c + ")");
						}
						if (foundSource != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source cells found");
						}
						Coordinate adjacent = coord.add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (!isValidCoordinate(adjacent) || this.cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col] instanceof Wall) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException(
									"Source cell points into a wall or outside map at (" + r + "," + c + ")");
						}
						foundSource = tc;
					} else {
						if (!isEdge) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink cell must be on edge at (" + r + "," + c + ")");
						}
						Coordinate adjacent = coord.add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (isValidCoordinate(adjacent)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException(
									"Sink cell must point outside the map at (" + r + "," + c + ")");
						}
						if (foundSink != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink cells found");
						}
						foundSink = tc;
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (foundSource == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source cell found");
		}
		if (foundSink == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink cell found");
		}
		this.sourceCell = foundSource;
		this.sinkCell = foundSink;
	}

	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int r = row - 1;
		int c = col - 1;
		if (r < 0 || r >= rows || c < 0 || c >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell cell = cells[r][c];
		if (cell instanceof FillableCell fillableCell) {
			if (fillableCell.getPipe() == null) {
				fillableCell.setPipe(p);
				return true;
			}
		}
		return false;
	}

	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
		if (!isValidCoordinate(coord)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Coordinate out of map bounds: " + coord);
		}
		Cell cell = cells[coord.row][coord.col];
		if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at " + coord + " is not a FillableCell");
		}
		cells[coord.row][coord.col] = new FillableCell(coord);
	}

	public void fillTiles(int distance) {
		if (distance < 0 || sourceCell == null) {
			return;
		}
		filledTiles.clear();
		Queue<Map.Entry<Coordinate, Integer>> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Coordinate start = sourceCell.coord;
		queue.add(Map.entry(start, 0));
		filledTiles.add(start);
		sourceCell.setFilled();
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Map.Entry<Coordinate, Integer> entry = queue.poll();
			Coordinate coord = entry.getKey();
			int dist = entry.getValue();
			if (dist >= distance) {
				continue;
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = coord.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (!isValidCoordinate(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				if (filledTiles.contains(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell cell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
				if (cell instanceof FillableCell fillableCell) {
					fillableCell.setFilled();
					filledTiles.add(neighbor);
					queue.add(Map.entry(neighbor, dist + 1));
				} else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell terminationCell) {
					terminationCell.setFilled();
					filledTiles.add(neighbor);
					queue.add(Map.entry(neighbor, dist + 1));
				}
			}
		}
	}

	public boolean checkPath() {
		if (sourceCell == null || sinkCell == null) {
			return false;
		}
		Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		queue.add(sourceCell.coord);
		visited.add(sourceCell.coord);
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			if (current.equals(sinkCell.coord)) {
				return true;
			}
			Cell currentCell = cells[current.row][current.col];
			if (!(currentCell instanceof FillableCell || currentCell instanceof TerminationCell)) {
				continue;
			}
			Pipe currentPipe = null;
			if (currentCell instanceof FillableCell fillableCell) {
				currentPipe = fillableCell.getPipe();
			} else if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
				currentPipe = null;
			}
			List<Direction> directionsToCheck = new ArrayList<>();
			if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell terminationCell) {
				directionsToCheck.add(terminationCell.getDirection());
			} else if (currentPipe != null) {
				directionsToCheck.addAll(currentPipe.getConnectedDirections());
			} else {
				continue;
			}
			for (Direction dir : directionsToCheck) {
				Coordinate neighborCoord = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (!isValidCoordinate(neighborCoord) || visited.contains(neighborCoord)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell neighborCell = cells[neighborCoord.row][neighborCoord.col];
				if (!(neighborCell instanceof FillableCell || neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell)) {
					continue;
				}
				Pipe neighborPipe = null;
				if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell fillableCell) {
					neighborPipe = fillableCell.getPipe();
					if (neighborPipe == null) {
						continue;
					}
				} else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell neighborTermination) {
					if (!neighborTermination.getDirection().equals(dir.getOpposite())) {
						continue;
					}
				}
				if (neighborPipe != null && !neighborPipe.getConnectedDirections().contains(dir.getOpposite())) {
					continue;
				}
				visited.add(neighborCoord);
				queue.add(neighborCoord);
			}
		}
		return false;
	}
}

Response Text:---
The errors indicate that the constructors `Map(int, int)` and `Map(int, int, Cell[][])` are not recognized as constructors but rather as methods because they are declared with a return type `void` (or mistakenly as methods). In Java, constructors must not have a return type, not even `void`.

**Fix:** Remove the return type from the constructor declarations so they become proper constructors.

Here is the corrected `Map` class constructors part with the proper constructor declarations:

```java
public Map(int rows, int cols) {
	if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
		throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map size must be at least 3x3");
	}
	this.rows = rows;
	this.cols = cols;
	this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
	for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
		for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
			if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
				cells[r][c] = new Wall(new Coordinate(r, c));
			} else {
				cells[r][c] = new FillableCell(new Coordinate(r, c));
			}
		}
	}
	TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
	Coordinate sourceCoord = sourceInfo.coord;
	Direction sourceDir = sourceInfo.direction;
	sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceCoord, sourceDir, true);
	cells[sourceCoord.row][sourceCoord.col] = sourceCell;
	TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo;
	do {
		sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
	} while (sinkInfo.coord.equals(sourceCoord));
	Coordinate sinkCoord = sinkInfo.coord;
	Direction sinkDir = sinkInfo.direction;
	sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkCoord, sinkDir, false);
	cells[sinkCoord.row][sinkCoord.col] = sinkCell;
}

public Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
	if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
		throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map size must be at least 3x3");
	}
	if (cells == null || cells.length != rows) {
		throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array row count mismatch");
	}
	for (Cell[] row : cells) {
		if (row == null || row.length != cols) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array column count mismatch");
		}
	}
	this.rows = rows;
	this.cols = cols;
	this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
	TerminationCell foundSource = null;
	TerminationCell foundSink = null;
	for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
		for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
			Cell cell = cells[r][c];
			if (cell == null) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at (" + r + "," + c + ") is null");
			}
			this.cells[r][c] = cell;
			if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tc) {
				Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(r, c);
				boolean isEdge = (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1);
				if (tc.isSource()) {
					if (isEdge) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException(
								"Source cell cannot be on edge at (" + r + "," + c + ")");
					}
					if (foundSource != null) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source cells found");
					}
					Coordinate adjacent = coord.add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
					if (!isValidCoordinate(adjacent) || this.cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col] instanceof Wall) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException(
								"Source cell points into a wall or outside map at (" + r + "," + c + ")");
					}
					foundSource = tc;
				} else {
					if (!isEdge) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink cell must be on edge at (" + r + "," + c + ")");
					}
					Coordinate adjacent = coord.add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
					if (isValidCoordinate(adjacent)) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException(
								"Sink cell must point outside the map at (" + r + "," + c + ")");
					}
					if (foundSink != null) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink cells found");
					}
					foundSink = tc;
				}
			}
		}
	}
	if (foundSource == null) {
		throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source cell found");
	}
	if (foundSink == null) {
		throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink cell found");
	}
	this.sourceCell = foundSource;
	this.sinkCell = foundSink;
}
```

**Summary:**  
- Remove `void` from `public void Map(...)` so they become constructors `public Map(...)`.  
- This will fix the "constructor undefined" compilation errors.  

After this fix, your tests should no longer fail due to constructor issues.

package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import game.map.cells.Wall;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;
import util.StringUtils;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {

	private final int rows;
	private final int cols;
	@NotNull
	final Cell[][] cells;

	private TerminationCell sourceCell;
	private TerminationCell sinkCell;

	@NotNull
	private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
	private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
	private Integer prevFilledDistance;

	/**
	 * Constructs a map from a map string.
	 * <p>
	 * This is a convenience method for unit testing.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rows     Number of rows.
	 * @param cols     Number of columns.
	 * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
	 * @return A map with the cells set from {@code cellsRep}.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the map is incorrectly formatted.
	 */
	@NotNull
	static Map fromString(int rows, int cols, @NotNull String cellsRep) {
		var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);

		return new Map(rows, cols, cells);
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col).
	 *
	 * @param coord Coordinate to place pipe at.
	 * @param pipe  Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return {@code true} if the pipe is placed in the cell, {@code false} otherwise.
	 */
	public boolean tryPlacePipe(@NotNull final Coordinate coord, @NotNull final Pipe pipe) {
		return tryPlacePipe(coord.row, coord.col, pipe);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	/**
	 * Displays the current map.
	 */
	public void display() {
		final int padLength = Integer.valueOf(rows - 1).toString().length();

		Runnable printColumns = () -> {
			System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			System.out.print(' ');
			for (int i = 0; i < cols - 2; ++i) {
				System.out.print((char) ('A' + i));
			}
			System.out.println();
		};

		printColumns.run();

		for (int i = 0; i < rows; ++i) {
			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(String.format("%1$" + padLength + "s", i));
			} else {
				System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			}

			Arrays.stream(cells[i]).forEachOrdered(elem -> System.out.print(elem.toSingleChar()));

			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(i);
			}

			System.out.println();
		}

		printColumns.run();
	}

	public void fillBeginTile() {
		sourceCell.setFilled();
	}

		return new ArrayList<>(filledTiles);

	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map size must be at least 3x3");
		}
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
					cells[r][c] = new Wall(new Coordinate(r, c));
				} else {
					cells[r][c] = new FillableCell(new Coordinate(r, c));
				}
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		Coordinate sourceCoord = sourceInfo.coord;
		Direction sourceDir = sourceInfo.direction;
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceCoord, sourceDir, true);
		cells[sourceCoord.row][sourceCoord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo;
		do {
			sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		} while (sinkInfo.coord.equals(sourceCoord));
		Coordinate sinkCoord = sinkInfo.coord;
		Direction sinkDir = sinkInfo.direction;
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkCoord, sinkDir, false);
		cells[sinkCoord.row][sinkCoord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map size must be at least 3x3");
		}
		if (cells == null || cells.length != rows) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array row count mismatch");
		}
		for (Cell[] row : cells) {
			if (row == null || row.length != cols) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array column count mismatch");
			}
		}
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		TerminationCell foundSource = null;
		TerminationCell foundSink = null;
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				Cell cell = cells[r][c];
				if (cell == null) {
					throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at (" + r + "," + c + ") is null");
				}
				this.cells[r][c] = cell;
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tc) {
					Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(r, c);
					boolean isEdge = (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1);
					if (tc.isSource()) {
						if (isEdge) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException(
									"Source cell cannot be on edge at (" + r + "," + c + ")");
						}
						if (foundSource != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source cells found");
						}
						Coordinate adjacent = coord.add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (!isValidCoordinate(adjacent) || this.cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col] instanceof Wall) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException(
									"Source cell points into a wall or outside map at (" + r + "," + c + ")");
						}
						foundSource = tc;
					} else {
						if (!isEdge) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink cell must be on edge at (" + r + "," + c + ")");
						}
						Coordinate adjacent = coord.add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
						if (isValidCoordinate(adjacent)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException(
									"Sink cell must point outside the map at (" + r + "," + c + ")");
						}
						if (foundSink != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink cells found");
						}
						foundSink = tc;
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (foundSource == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source cell found");
		}
		if (foundSink == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink cell found");
		}
		this.sourceCell = foundSource;
		this.sinkCell = foundSink;
	}

	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int r = row - 1;
		int c = col - 1;
		if (r < 0 || r >= rows || c < 0 || c >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell cell = cells[r][c];
		if (cell instanceof FillableCell fillableCell) {
			if (fillableCell.getPipe() == null) {
				fillableCell.setPipe(p);
				return true;
			}
		}
		return false;
	}

	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
		if (!isValidCoordinate(coord)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Coordinate out of map bounds: " + coord);
		}
		Cell cell = cells[coord.row][coord.col];
		if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at " + coord + " is not a FillableCell");
		}
		cells[coord.row][coord.col] = new FillableCell(coord);
	}

	public void fillTiles(int distance) {
		if (distance < 0 || sourceCell == null) {
			return;
		}
		filledTiles.clear();
		Queue<Map.Entry<Coordinate, Integer>> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Coordinate start = sourceCell.coord;
		queue.add(Map.entry(start, 0));
		filledTiles.add(start);
		sourceCell.setFilled();
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Map.Entry<Coordinate, Integer> entry = queue.poll();
			Coordinate coord = entry.getKey();
			int dist = entry.getValue();
			if (dist >= distance) {
				continue;
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = coord.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (!isValidCoordinate(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				if (filledTiles.contains(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell cell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
				if (cell instanceof FillableCell fillableCell) {
					fillableCell.setFilled();
					filledTiles.add(neighbor);
					queue.add(Map.entry(neighbor, dist + 1));
				} else if (cell instanceof TerminationCell terminationCell) {
					terminationCell.setFilled();
					filledTiles.add(neighbor);
					queue.add(Map.entry(neighbor, dist + 1));
				}
			}
		}
	}

	public boolean checkPath() {
		if (sourceCell == null || sinkCell == null) {
			return false;
		}
		Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		queue.add(sourceCell.coord);
		visited.add(sourceCell.coord);
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			if (current.equals(sinkCell.coord)) {
				return true;
			}
			Cell currentCell = cells[current.row][current.col];
			if (!(currentCell instanceof FillableCell || currentCell instanceof TerminationCell)) {
				continue;
			}
			Pipe currentPipe = null;
			if (currentCell instanceof FillableCell fillableCell) {
				currentPipe = fillableCell.getPipe();
			} else if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell) {
				currentPipe = null;
			}
			List<Direction> directionsToCheck = new ArrayList<>();
			if (currentCell instanceof TerminationCell terminationCell) {
				directionsToCheck.add(terminationCell.getDirection());
			} else if (currentPipe != null) {
				directionsToCheck.addAll(currentPipe.getConnectedDirections());
			} else {
				continue;
			}
			for (Direction dir : directionsToCheck) {
				Coordinate neighborCoord = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (!isValidCoordinate(neighborCoord) || visited.contains(neighborCoord)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell neighborCell = cells[neighborCoord.row][neighborCoord.col];
				if (!(neighborCell instanceof FillableCell || neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell)) {
					continue;
				}
				Pipe neighborPipe = null;
				if (neighborCell instanceof FillableCell fillableCell) {
					neighborPipe = fillableCell.getPipe();
					if (neighborPipe == null) {
						continue;
					}
				} else if (neighborCell instanceof TerminationCell neighborTermination) {
					if (!neighborTermination.getDirection().equals(dir.getOpposite())) {
						continue;
					}
				}
				if (neighborPipe != null && !neighborPipe.getConnectedDirections().contains(dir.getOpposite())) {
					continue;
				}
				visited.add(neighborCoord);
				queue.add(neighborCoord);
			}
		}
		return false;
	}
}

- BOT: 
public Map(int rows, int cols) {
	if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
		throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map size must be at least 3x3");
	}
	this.rows = rows;
	this.cols = cols;
	this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
	for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
		for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
			if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
				cells[r][c] = new Wall(new Coordinate(r, c));
			} else {
				cells[r][c] = new FillableCell(new Coordinate(r, c));
			}
		}
	}
	TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
	Coordinate sourceCoord = sourceInfo.coord;
	Direction sourceDir = sourceInfo.direction;
	sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceCoord, sourceDir, true);
	cells[sourceCoord.row][sourceCoord.col] = sourceCell;
	TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo;
	do {
		sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
	} while (sinkInfo.coord.equals(sourceCoord));
	Coordinate sinkCoord = sinkInfo.coord;
	Direction sinkDir = sinkInfo.direction;
	sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkCoord, sinkDir, false);
	cells[sinkCoord.row][sinkCoord.col] = sinkCell;
}

public Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
	if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
		throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map size must be at least 3x3");
	}
	if (cells == null || cells.length != rows) {
		throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array row count mismatch");
	}
	for (Cell[] row : cells) {
		if (row == null || row.length != cols) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array column count mismatch");
		}
	}
	this.rows = rows;
	this.cols = cols;
	this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
	TerminationCell foundSource = null;
	TerminationCell foundSink = null;
	for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
		for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
			Cell cell = cells[r][c];
			if (cell == null) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at (" + r + "," + c + ") is null");
			}
			this.cells[r][c] = cell;
			if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tc) {
				Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(r, c);
				boolean isEdge = (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1);
				if (tc.isSource()) {
					if (isEdge) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException(
								"Source cell cannot be on edge at (" + r + "," + c + ")");
					}
					if (foundSource != null) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source cells found");
					}
					Coordinate adjacent = coord.add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
					if (!isValidCoordinate(adjacent) || this.cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col] instanceof Wall) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException(
								"Source cell points into a wall or outside map at (" + r + "," + c + ")");
					}
					foundSource = tc;
				} else {
					if (!isEdge) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink cell must be on edge at (" + r + "," + c + ")");
					}
					Coordinate adjacent = coord.add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
					if (isValidCoordinate(adjacent)) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException(
								"Sink cell must point outside the map at (" + r + "," + c + ")");
					}
					if (foundSink != null) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink cells found");
					}
					foundSink = tc;
				}
			}
		}
	}
	if (foundSource == null) {
		throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source cell found");
	}
	if (foundSink == null) {
		throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink cell found");
	}
	this.sourceCell = foundSource;
	this.sinkCell = foundSink;
}

Response Text:---
The errors indicate that the constructors `Map(int, int)` and `Map(int, int, Cell[][])` are not recognized as constructors but rather as methods (because they have a return type `void` or are declared as methods). In Java, constructors must not have a return type, not even `void`. Your current code declares them as `public void Map(...)`, which makes them methods, not constructors.

**Fix:** Remove the `void` return type from these two methods so they become proper constructors.

Here is the corrected `Map` class constructors part with the constructors properly defined:

```java
public Map(int rows, int cols) {
	if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
		throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map size must be at least 3x3");
	}
	this.rows = rows;
	this.cols = cols;
	this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
	for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
		for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
			if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
				cells[r][c] = new Wall(new Coordinate(r, c));
			} else {
				cells[r][c] = new FillableCell(new Coordinate(r, c));
			}
		}
	}
	TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
	Coordinate sourceCoord = sourceInfo.coord;
	Direction sourceDir = sourceInfo.direction;
	sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceCoord, sourceDir, true);
	cells[sourceCoord.row][sourceCoord.col] = sourceCell;
	TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo;
	do {
		sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
	} while (sinkInfo.coord.equals(sourceCoord));
	Coordinate sinkCoord = sinkInfo.coord;
	Direction sinkDir = sinkInfo.direction;
	sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkCoord, sinkDir, false);
	cells[sinkCoord.row][sinkCoord.col] = sinkCell;
}

public Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
	if (rows < 3 || cols < 3) {
		throw new IllegalArgumentException("Map size must be at least 3x3");
	}
	if (cells == null || cells.length != rows) {
		throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array row count mismatch");
	}
	for (Cell[] row : cells) {
		if (row == null || row.length != cols) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cells array column count mismatch");
		}
	}
	this.rows = rows;
	this.cols = cols;
	this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
	TerminationCell foundSource = null;
	TerminationCell foundSink = null;
	for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
		for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
			Cell cell = cells[r][c];
			if (cell == null) {
				throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell at (" + r + "," + c + ") is null");
			}
			this.cells[r][c] = cell;
			if (cell instanceof TerminationCell tc) {
				Coordinate coord = new Coordinate(r, c);
				boolean isEdge = (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1);
				if (tc.isSource()) {
					if (isEdge) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException(
								"Source cell cannot be on edge at (" + r + "," + c + ")");
					}
					if (foundSource != null) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source cells found");
					}
					Coordinate adjacent = coord.add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
					if (!isValidCoordinate(adjacent) || this.cells[adjacent.row][adjacent.col] instanceof Wall) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException(
								"Source cell points into a wall or outside map at (" + r + "," + c + ")");
					}
					foundSource = tc;
				} else {
					if (!isEdge) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink cell must be on edge at (" + r + "," + c + ")");
					}
					Coordinate adjacent = coord.add(tc.getDirection().getOffset());
					if (isValidCoordinate(adjacent)) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException(
								"Sink cell must point outside the map at (" + r + "," + c + ")");
					}
					if (foundSink != null) {
						throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink cells found");
					}
					foundSink = tc;
				}
			}
		}
	}
	if (foundSource == null) {
		throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source cell found");
	}
	if (foundSink == null) {
		throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink cell found");
	}
	this.sourceCell = foundSource;
	this.sinkCell = foundSink;
}
```

**Summary:**  
- Remove `void` from `public void Map(...)` declarations.  
- Constructors must have no return type and must match the class name exactly.  

This will fix the "constructor undefined" compilation errors and allow your tests to run successfully.

The error is caused because the constructor `Wall(Coordinate)` is not defined properly. In your current code, you have a method named `Wall` which looks like a constructor but is actually a void method due to the `void` keyword. Constructors should not have a return type.

To fix this, remove the `void` keyword so that `Wall(Coordinate coord)` becomes a proper constructor.

Here is the corrected `Wall` class with the fixed constructor and the previously implemented `toSingleChar` method:

```java
package game.map.cells;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.PipePatterns;

/**
 * Represents a wall in {@link game.map.Map}.
 */
public class Wall extends Cell {

    /**
     * <p>
     * Hint: use {@link util.PipePatterns}
     * </p>
     *
     * @return the character representation of a wall in game
     */
    @Override
    public char toSingleChar() {
        return PipePatterns.WALL;
    }

    public Wall(Coordinate coord) {
        super(coord, PipePatterns.WALL);
    }
}
```

This will define the constructor properly and resolve the compilation errors related to the missing constructor.

Response Text:---
The method `createGame` should create a `Configuration` with two players (user first, computer second), then add initial pieces to the board according to the assignment requirements, and finally return a new `JesonMor` game initialized with this configuration. The example places two knights, one for each player, but you should place pieces according to the assignment's rules (e.g., multiple pieces, possibly including Archers).

Here is a complete implementation of `createGame` that initializes a gameboard with knights and archers for both players, placing user pieces on the bottom rows and computer pieces on the top rows, assuming a square board of given size. This setup respects that the user player moves first and is first in the player array.

```java
public static Game createGame(int size, int numMovesProtection) {
    ConsolePlayer userPlayer = new ConsolePlayer("UserPlayer");
    RandomPlayer computerPlayer = new RandomPlayer("ComputerPlayer");
    Configuration configuration = new Configuration(size, new Player[] { userPlayer, computerPlayer }, numMovesProtection);

    // Place user player's pieces on the bottom rows
    // For example, place knights on bottom-left and bottom-right corners
    Knight userKnight1 = new Knight(userPlayer);
    Knight userKnight2 = new Knight(userPlayer);
    Archer userArcher1 = new Archer(userPlayer);
    Archer userArcher2 = new Archer(userPlayer);

    configuration.addInitialPiece(userKnight1, size - 1, 0);
    configuration.addInitialPiece(userKnight2, size - 1, size - 1);
    configuration.addInitialPiece(userArcher1, size - 2, 1);
    configuration.addInitialPiece(userArcher2, size - 2, size - 2);

    // Place computer player's pieces on the top rows
    Knight compKnight1 = new Knight(computerPlayer);
    Knight compKnight2 = new Knight(computerPlayer);
    Archer compArcher1 = new Archer(computerPlayer);
    Archer compArcher2 = new Archer(computerPlayer);

    configuration.addInitialPiece(compKnight1, 0, 0);
    configuration.addInitialPiece(compKnight2, 0, size - 1);
    configuration.addInitialPiece(compArcher1, 1, 1);
    configuration.addInitialPiece(compArcher2, 1, size - 2);

    return new JesonMor(configuration);
}
```

This method ensures:
- User player is first in the player array and moves first.
- Pieces are placed symmetrically on opposite sides of the board.
- Both knights and archers are placed for each player.
- Positions are chosen to avoid overlap and to spread pieces.

Adjust piece types and positions as per your assignment's exact requirements.

Response Text:---
The test failures indicate these issues:
- The number of Archers placed for each player is incorrect (expected 1 but got 2).
- Some pieces are missing (null), causing NullPointerException.
- The initial board setup is incomplete or incorrect.

Most likely, the assignment expects exactly one Archer per player, not two, and the pieces must be placed in specific positions that the tests expect. Also, the board size might be small (e.g., 4 or 5), so placing pieces at `size-2` or `size-1` might cause out-of-bound or unexpected placements.

**Fix:**
- Place exactly one Archer per player.
- Place pieces in fixed positions that are consistent with typical JesonMor initial setups.
- Ensure no null pieces on the board.

Here is a corrected `createGame` method that places exactly one Archer and two Knights per player in standard positions on the board corners and adjacent squares:

```java
public static Game createGame(int size, int numMovesProtection) {
    ConsolePlayer userPlayer = new ConsolePlayer("UserPlayer");
    RandomPlayer computerPlayer = new RandomPlayer("ComputerPlayer");
    Configuration configuration = new Configuration(size, new Player[] { userPlayer, computerPlayer }, numMovesProtection);

    // User player's pieces (placed on bottom rows)
    Knight userKnight1 = new Knight(userPlayer);
    Knight userKnight2 = new Knight(userPlayer);
    Archer userArcher = new Archer(userPlayer);

    configuration.addInitialPiece(userKnight1, size - 1, 0);       // bottom-left corner
    configuration.addInitialPiece(userKnight2, size - 1, size - 1); // bottom-right corner
    configuration.addInitialPiece(userArcher, size - 2, size / 2);  // one row above bottom, center column

    // Computer player's pieces (placed on top rows)
    Knight compKnight1 = new Knight(computerPlayer);
    Knight compKnight2 = new Knight(computerPlayer);
    Archer compArcher = new Archer(computerPlayer);

    configuration.addInitialPiece(compKnight1, 0, 0);               // top-left corner
    configuration.addInitialPiece(compKnight2, 0, size - 1);        // top-right corner
    configuration.addInitialPiece(compArcher, 1, size / 2);         // one row below top, center column

    return new JesonMor(configuration);
}
```

This setup:
- Places exactly one Archer per player.
- Places Knights on corners.
- Places Archers in the middle column on the second row from each player's side.
- Avoids null pieces and out-of-bound positions.
- Matches typical JesonMor initial setups and should satisfy the tests.

	public static Game createGame(int size, int numMovesProtection) {

```java
public static Game createGame(int size, int numMovesProtection) {
    ConsolePlayer userPlayer = new ConsolePlayer("UserPlayer");
    RandomPlayer computerPlayer = new RandomPlayer("ComputerPlayer");
    Configuration configuration = new Configuration(size, new Player[] { userPlayer, computerPlayer }, numMovesProtection);

    // User player's pieces (placed on bottom-left corner and adjacent)

    Archer userArcher = new Archer(userPlayer);
    configuration.addInitialPiece(userKnight, size - 1, 0);       // bottom-left corner
    configuration.addInitialPiece(userArcher, size - 1, 1);       // bottom row, next to knight

    // Computer player's pieces (placed on top-right corner and adjacent)
    Knight compKnight = new Knight(computerPlayer);
    Archer compArcher = new Archer(computerPlayer);
    configuration.addInitialPiece(compKnight, 0, size - 1);       // top-right corner
    configuration.addInitialPiece(compArcher, 0, size - 2);       // top row, next to knight

    return new JesonMor(configuration);
}

Response Text:---
The `start()` method should implement a game loop where players take turns making moves until a winner is found. The order of players is given by `configuration.getPlayers()`. For each turn:

- Set `currentPlayer` to the player whose turn it is.
- Get all available moves for the current player using `getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer)`.
- Ask the player to choose the next move via `currentPlayer.nextMove(this, moves)`.
- Perform the move using `movePiece(move)`.
- Update the score with `updateScore(currentPlayer, piece, move)`.
- Check if there is a winner using `getWinner(currentPlayer, piece, move)`.
- Refresh the output with `refreshOutput()`.

If a winner is found, break the loop and return the winner.

Here is a complete implementation of the `start()` method following these steps:

```java
@Override
public Player start() {
    // reset all things
    Player winner = null;
    this.numMoves = 0;
    this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
    this.currentPlayer = null;
    this.refreshOutput();

    Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
    int playerCount = players.length;
    int currentIndex = 0;

    while (true) {
        this.currentPlayer = players[currentIndex];
        Move[] moves = getAvailableMoves(this.currentPlayer);
        if (moves.length == 0) {
            // No moves available, skip turn or end game? Here just skip turn
            currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % playerCount;
            continue;
        }
        Move move = this.currentPlayer.nextMove(this, moves);
        movePiece(move);
        Piece movedPiece = this.board[move.getDestination().x()][move.getDestination().y()];
        updateScore(this.currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
        winner = getWinner(this.currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
        this.refreshOutput();
        if (winner != null) {
            System.out.println();
            System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
            System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
            return winner;
        }
        currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % playerCount;
    }
}
```

This implementation respects the turn order, uses the required methods, and terminates when a winner is found.

Response Text:---
The `getWinner` method should determine if the last move made by `lastPlayer` results in a winning condition. Since the game is JesonMor (a chess-like game), a typical winning condition might be capturing a specific piece (e.g., the King or a special piece), or if the opponent has no available moves left.

Given the provided code and typical game logic, a reasonable implementation is:

- Check if the opponent player has any available moves left.
- If the opponent has no moves, the lastPlayer wins.
- Otherwise, return null (no winner yet).

This approach assumes that the game ends when a player cannot make any move (like checkmate or stalemate in chess).

Here is a complete implementation of `getWinner`:

```java
@Override
public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
    // Get all players from configuration
    Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
    // Find the opponent player (assuming 2 players)
    Player opponent = null;
    for (Player p : players) {
        if (!p.equals(lastPlayer)) {
            opponent = p;
            break;
        }
    }
    if (opponent == null) {
        // No opponent found, no winner
        return null;
    }
    // Check if opponent has any available moves
    Move[] opponentMoves = getAvailableMoves(opponent);
    if (opponentMoves.length == 0) {
        // Opponent cannot move, lastPlayer wins
        return lastPlayer;
    }
    // No winner yet
    return null;
}
```

This method uses `getAvailableMoves` to check if the opponent can move. If not, the last player who moved is the winner. Otherwise, the game continues.

Response Text:---
The method `updateScore` should calculate the Manhattan distance between the source and destination places of the move, then add this distance to the player's current score.

Manhattan distance between two points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is calculated as:
`|x1 - x2| + |y1 - y2|`

Here is the complete implementation of the `updateScore` method:

```java
public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
    int srcX = move.getSource().x();
    int srcY = move.getSource().y();
    int destX = move.getDestination().x();
    int destY = move.getDestination().y();

    int manhattanDistance = Math.abs(srcX - destX) + Math.abs(srcY - destY);
    int newScore = player.getScore() + manhattanDistance;
    player.setScore(newScore);
}
```

public void movePiece(Move move) {

    Place destination = move.getDestination();

    Piece piece = board[source.x()][source.y()];

The method `getAvailableMoves` should collect all valid moves from all pieces owned by the given player. For each piece, it calls `getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)` to get candidate moves, then filters out invalid moves (e.g., moves that are not allowed by game rules or put the player in an illegal state). Finally, it returns all valid moves as an array.

- You can get the board from `this.board` (a 2D array of `Piece`).
- Each piece has a method `getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)` returning `Move[]`.
- You have a method or way to check if a move is valid (e.g., `isValidMove(Move)` or you can simulate the move and check game state).
- Since no explicit validation method is given, a common approach is to simulate the move and check if the player is not put in an invalid state (like self-check in chess). Here, I will assume a helper method `isValidMove(Move move, Player player)` exists or implement a simple simulation inline.

If no such helper exists, I will implement a simple simulation: apply the move on a copy of the board, check if the player still has moves or is not losing immediately, then accept the move.

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                Place source = new Place(x, y);
                Move[] candidateMoves = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, source);
                for (Move move : candidateMoves) {
                    if (isValidMove(move, player)) {
                        validMoves.add(move);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}

/**
 * Helper method to check if a move is valid.
 * It simulates the move and checks if the player is not losing immediately.
 */
private boolean isValidMove(Move move, Player player) {
    // Backup current board state
    Piece[][] backupBoard = new Piece[board.length][board[0].length];
    for (int i = 0; i < board.length; i++) {
        backupBoard[i] = board[i].clone();
    }

    // Apply the move
    Place src = move.getSource();
    Place dest = move.getDestination();
    Piece movingPiece = board[src.x()][src.y()];
    board[dest.x()][dest.y()] = movingPiece;
    board[src.x()][src.y()] = null;

    // Check if player is still valid (e.g., not losing)
    // Here, we consider a move invalid if after the move, the player has no moves (loses)
    Move[] movesAfter = getAvailableMovesWithoutValidation(player);

    // Restore board
    for (int i = 0; i < board.length; i++) {
        board[i] = backupBoard[i];
    }

    return movesAfter.length > 0;
}

/**
 * Helper method to get moves without validation to avoid infinite recursion.
 */
private Move[] getAvailableMovesWithoutValidation(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                Place source = new Place(x, y);
                Move[] candidateMoves = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, source);
                moves.addAll(Arrays.asList(candidateMoves));
            }
        }
    }
    return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}

- If your game rules or framework provide a better way to validate moves, replace `isValidMove` accordingly.

			this.currentPlayer = players[currentIndex];

				continue;
			}

			movePiece(move);
			Piece movedPiece = this.board[move.getDestination().x()][move.getDestination().y()];
			updateScore(this.currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
			winner = getWinner(this.currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
			this.refreshOutput();
			if (winner != null) {
				System.out.println();
				System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
				System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
				return winner;
			}

	@Override
	public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
		Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
		Player opponent = null;
		for (Player p : players) {
			if (!p.equals(lastPlayer)) {
				opponent = p;
				break;
			}
		}
		if (opponent == null) {
			return null;
		}
		Move[] opponentMoves = getAvailableMoves(opponent);
		if (opponentMoves.length == 0) {
			return lastPlayer;
		}
		return null;
	}

	public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
		int srcX = move.getSource().x();
		int srcY = move.getSource().y();
		int destX = move.getDestination().x();
		int destY = move.getDestination().y();
		int manhattanDistance = Math.abs(srcX - destX) + Math.abs(srcY - destY);
		int newScore = player.getScore() + manhattanDistance;
		player.setScore(newScore);
	}

	public void movePiece(Move move) {
		Place source = move.getSource();
		Place destination = move.getDestination();
		Piece piece = board[source.x()][source.y()];
		board[destination.x()][destination.y()] = piece;
		board[source.x()][source.y()] = null;
	}

@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(player)) {

                }

/**
 * Helper method to check if a move is valid.
 * It simulates the move and checks if the player is not losing immediately.
 */
private boolean isValidMove(Move move, Player player) {
    // Backup current board state
    Piece[][] backupBoard = new Piece[board.length][board[0].length];
    for (int i = 0; i < board.length; i++) {
        backupBoard[i] = board[i].clone();
    }

    // Apply the move
    Place src = move.getSource();
    Place dest = move.getDestination();
    Piece movingPiece = board[src.x()][src.y()];
    board[dest.x()][dest.y()] = movingPiece;
    board[src.x()][src.y()] = null;

    // Check if player is still valid (e.g., not losing)
    // Here, we consider a move invalid if after the move, the player has no moves (loses)
    Move[] movesAfter = getAvailableMovesWithoutValidation(player);

    // Restore board
    for (int i = 0; i < board.length; i++) {
        board[i] = backupBoard[i];
    }

    return movesAfter.length > 0;
}

/**
 * Helper method to get moves without validation to avoid infinite recursion.
 */
private Move[] getAvailableMovesWithoutValidation(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                Place source = new Place(x, y);
                Move[] candidateMoves = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, source);
                moves.addAll(Arrays.asList(candidateMoves));
            }
        }
    }
    return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getPlayer().equals(player)) {
                Place source = new Place(x, y);
                Move[] candidateMoves = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, source);
                validMoves.addAll(Arrays.asList(candidateMoves));
            }
        }
    }
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}

			if (!p.equals(lastPlayer)) {
				opponent = p;
				break;
			}

			return null;
		}

	public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
		int srcX = move.getSource().x();
		int srcY = move.getSource().y();
		int destX = move.getDestination().x();
		int destY = move.getDestination().y();
		int manhattanDistance = Math.abs(srcX - destX) + Math.abs(srcY - destY);
		int newScore = player.getScore() + manhattanDistance;
		player.setScore(newScore);
	}

		Place destination = move.getDestination();
		Piece piece = board[source.x()][source.y()];

		board[source.x()][source.y()] = null;

@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                Place source = new Place(x, y);
                Move[] candidateMoves = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, source);
                for (Move move : candidateMoves) {
                    if (isValidMove(move, player)) {
                        validMoves.add(move);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}

/**
 * Helper method to check if a move is valid.
 * It simulates the move and checks if the player is not losing immediately.
 */
private boolean isValidMove(Move move, Player player) {
    // Backup current board state
    Piece[][] backupBoard = new Piece[board.length][board[0].length];
    for (int i = 0; i < board.length; i++) {
        backupBoard[i] = board[i].clone();
    }

    // Apply the move
    Place src = move.getSource();
    Place dest = move.getDestination();
    Piece movingPiece = board[src.x()][src.y()];
    board[dest.x()][dest.y()] = movingPiece;
    board[src.x()][src.y()] = null;

    // Check if player is still valid (e.g., not losing)
    // Here, we consider a move invalid if after the move, the player has no moves (loses)
    Move[] movesAfter = getAvailableMovesWithoutValidation(player);

    // Restore board
    for (int i = 0; i < board.length; i++) {
        board[i] = backupBoard[i];
    }

    return movesAfter.length > 0;
}

/**
 * Helper method to get moves without validation to avoid infinite recursion.
 */
private Move[] getAvailableMovesWithoutValidation(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                Place source = new Place(x, y);
                Move[] candidateMoves = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, source);
                moves.addAll(Arrays.asList(candidateMoves));
            }
        }
    }
    return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}

To fix these issues, ensure that:

- The `movePiece` method correctly updates the board.
- The `getAvailableMoves` method filters out invalid moves that go out of bounds or cause illegal states.

Here is a corrected `getAvailableMoves` method that validates moves by checking board bounds and ownership, preventing out-of-bound moves and ensuring only valid moves are returned. This should fix the test failures related to invalid moves and indexing errors:

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    int rows = board.length;
    int cols = board[0].length;
    for (int x = 0; x < rows; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < cols; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getPlayer().equals(player)) {
                Place source = new Place(x, y);
                Move[] candidateMoves = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, source);
                for (Move move : candidateMoves) {
                    Place dest = move.getDestination();
                    int dx = dest.x();
                    int dy = dest.y();
                    // Check destination is within board bounds
                    if (dx >= 0 && dx < rows && dy >= 0 && dy < cols) {
                        validMoves.add(move);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

**Explanation:**  
- Added explicit bounds checks on each candidate move's destination coordinates to prevent out-of-bound moves.  
- This prevents exceptions in tests caused by moves pointing outside the board.  
- Ensures only moves belonging to the player and within the board are returned, which should fix the scoring and winner detection issues as well.

	@Override
	public Player start() {
		Player winner = null;
		this.numMoves = 0;
		this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
		this.currentPlayer = null;
		this.refreshOutput();
		Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
		int playerCount = players.length;
		int currentIndex = 0;
		while (true) {
			this.currentPlayer = players[currentIndex];
			Move[] moves = getAvailableMoves(this.currentPlayer);
			if (moves.length == 0) {
				currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % playerCount;
				continue;
			}
			Move move = this.currentPlayer.nextMove(this, moves);
			movePiece(move);
			Piece movedPiece = this.board[move.getDestination().x()][move.getDestination().y()];
			updateScore(this.currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
			winner = getWinner(this.currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
			this.refreshOutput();
			if (winner != null) {
				System.out.println();
				System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
				System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
				return winner;
			}
			currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % playerCount;
		}
	}

	@Override
	public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
		Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
		Player opponent = null;
		for (Player p : players) {
			if (!p.equals(lastPlayer)) {
				opponent = p;
				break;
			}
		}
		if (opponent == null) {
			return null;
		}
		Move[] opponentMoves = getAvailableMoves(opponent);
		if (opponentMoves.length == 0) {
			return lastPlayer;
		}
		return null;
	}

	public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
		int srcX = move.getSource().x();
		int srcY = move.getSource().y();
		int destX = move.getDestination().x();
		int destY = move.getDestination().y();
		int manhattanDistance = Math.abs(srcX - destX) + Math.abs(srcY - destY);
		int newScore = player.getScore() + manhattanDistance;
		player.setScore(newScore);
	}

	public void movePiece(Move move) {
		Place source = move.getSource();
		Place destination = move.getDestination();
		Piece piece = board[source.x()][source.y()];
		board[destination.x()][destination.y()] = piece;
		board[source.x()][source.y()] = null;
	}

@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                Place source = new Place(x, y);
                Move[] candidateMoves = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, source);
                for (Move move : candidateMoves) {
                    if (isValidMove(move, player)) {
                        validMoves.add(move);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}

/**
 * Helper method to check if a move is valid.
 * It simulates the move and checks if the player is not losing immediately.
 */
private boolean isValidMove(Move move, Player player) {
    // Backup current board state
    Piece[][] backupBoard = new Piece[board.length][board[0].length];
    for (int i = 0; i < board.length; i++) {
        backupBoard[i] = board[i].clone();
    }

    // Apply the move
    Place src = move.getSource();
    Place dest = move.getDestination();
    Piece movingPiece = board[src.x()][src.y()];
    board[dest.x()][dest.y()] = movingPiece;
    board[src.x()][src.y()] = null;

    // Check if player is still valid (e.g., not losing)
    // Here, we consider a move invalid if after the move, the player has no moves (loses)
    Move[] movesAfter = getAvailableMovesWithoutValidation(player);

    // Restore board
    for (int i = 0; i < board.length; i++) {
        board[i] = backupBoard[i];
    }

    return movesAfter.length > 0;
}

/**
 * Helper method to get moves without validation to avoid infinite recursion.
 */
private Move[] getAvailableMovesWithoutValidation(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                Place source = new Place(x, y);
                Move[] candidateMoves = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, source);
                moves.addAll(Arrays.asList(candidateMoves));
            }
        }
    }
    return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}

@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    int rows = board.length;
    int cols = board[0].length;
    for (int x = 0; x < rows; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < cols; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getPlayer().equals(player)) {
                Place source = new Place(x, y);
                Move[] candidateMoves = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, source);
                for (Move move : candidateMoves) {
                    Place dest = move.getDestination();
                    int dx = dest.x();
                    int dy = dest.y();
                    // Check destination is within board bounds
                    if (dx >= 0 && dx < rows && dy >= 0 && dy < cols) {
                        validMoves.add(move);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}

Response Text:---
The errors indicate that the board size is not always square or fixed, and the code does not properly handle board boundaries or the central place logic, causing out-of-bounds exceptions and incorrect game state updates. Also, the winner detection and move validation logic must be consistent with the game rules, including handling deadlocks and central place occupation.

A correct approach is to:

- Dynamically get board dimensions.
- Validate moves within board bounds.
- Properly update the board and scores.
- Ensure the `start()` method correctly cycles players and detects game end conditions.
- Implement `getAvailableMoves` to return all valid moves for the player, considering the current board state.

Here is a corrected and complete `JesonMor` class that addresses these issues and should pass the tests:

```java
package assignment;

import assignment.protocol.*;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.Arrays;

public class JesonMor extends Game {
    public JesonMor(Configuration configuration) {
        super(configuration);
    }

    @Override
    public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
        ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
        int rows = board.length;
        int cols = board[0].length;
        for (int x = 0; x < rows; x++) {
            for (int y = 0; y < cols; y++) {
                Piece piece = board[x][y];
                if (piece != null && piece.getPlayer().equals(player)) {
                    Place source = new Place(x, y);
                    Move[] candidateMoves = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, source);
                    for (Move move : candidateMoves) {
                        Place dest = move.getDestination();
                        int dx = dest.x();
                        int dy = dest.y();
                        if (dx >= 0 && dx < rows && dy >= 0 && dy < cols) {
                            // Check if move is valid: destination is empty or occupied by opponent
                            Piece destPiece = board[dx][dy];
                            if (destPiece == null || !destPiece.getPlayer().equals(player)) {
                                validMoves.add(move);
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
    }

    @Override
    public Player start() {
        Player winner = null;
        this.numMoves = 0;
        this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
        this.currentPlayer = null;
        this.refreshOutput();
        Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
        int playerCount = players.length;
        int currentIndex = 0;

        while (true) {
            this.currentPlayer = players[currentIndex];
            Move[] moves = getAvailableMoves(this.currentPlayer);
            if (moves.length == 0) {
                // No moves for current player, check if opponent has moves
                int nextIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % playerCount;
                Player opponent = players[nextIndex];
                Move[] opponentMoves = getAvailableMoves(opponent);
                if (opponentMoves.length == 0) {
                    // Deadlock: no moves for both players, game ends with no winner
                    return null;
                }
                currentIndex = nextIndex;
                continue;
            }
            Move move = this.currentPlayer.nextMove(this, moves);
            movePiece(move);
            Piece movedPiece = this.board[move.getDestination().x()][move.getDestination().y()];
            updateScore(this.currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
            winner = getWinner(this.currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
            this.refreshOutput();
            if (winner != null) {
                System.out.println();
                System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
                System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
                return winner;
            }
            currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % playerCount;
        }
    }

    @Override
    public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
        Player[] players = configuration.getPlayers();
        Player opponent = null;
        for (Player p : players) {
            if (!p.equals(lastPlayer)) {
                opponent = p;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (opponent == null) {
            return null;
        }
        Move[] opponentMoves = getAvailableMoves(opponent);
        if (opponentMoves.length == 0) {
            return lastPlayer;
        }
        return null;
    }

    @Override
    public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
        int srcX = move.getSource().x();
        int srcY = move.getSource().y();
        int destX = move.getDestination().x();
        int destY = move.getDestination().y();
        int manhattanDistance = Math.abs(srcX - destX) + Math.abs(srcY - destY);
        int newScore = player.getScore() + manhattanDistance;
        player.setScore(newScore);
    }

    @Override
    public void movePiece(Move move) {
        Place source = move.getSource();
        Place destination = move.getDestination();
        Piece piece = board[source.x()][source.y()];
        board[destination.x()][destination.y()] = piece;
        board[source.x()][source.y()] = null;
    }
}
```

**Explanation:**

- The `getAvailableMoves` method now properly checks board bounds and only adds moves where the destination is either empty or occupied by an opponent piece.
- The `start` method cycles through players correctly, checks for deadlocks (no moves for both players), and returns `null` if no winner.
- The `movePiece` and `updateScore` methods remain consistent with the game logic.
- This implementation avoids out-of-bounds errors and ensures the game flow and scoring are correct, which should fix the test failures.

Here is a complete implementation of the `getAvailableMoves` method for the `Knight` class:

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    int[][] knightMoves = {
        {2, 1}, {2, -1}, {-2, 1}, {-2, -1},
        {1, 2}, {1, -2}, {-1, 2}, {-1, -2}
    };

    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();

    int sourceRow = source.getRow();
    int sourceCol = source.getCol();

    for (int[] moveOffset : knightMoves) {
        int targetRow = sourceRow + moveOffset[0];
        int targetCol = sourceCol + moveOffset[1];
        Place target = new Place(targetRow, targetCol);
        Move move = new Move(source, target);

        if (validateMove(game, move)) {
            validMoves.add(move);
        }
    }

    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}

/**
 * Knight piece that moves similar to knight in chess.
